MCCHEAM212.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
MCCHEAM212.contribution: Examines Renaissance art across Europe and the Mediterranean, including connections with Islamic courts.
MCCHEAM212.topics: This course examines the painting, sculpture, and architecture of Renaissance Italy and the extensive artistic connections that linked the Italian peninsula to other regions of the world. By exploring a range of geographical contexts, from the Islamic courts of the Eastern Mediterranean and the commercial routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa to the newly encountered territories of the Americas, students will examine how trade, colonization, and cross-cultural exchange shaped the production and meaning of Renaissance art.

MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.contribution: Develops historical and methodological inquiry into aesthetics and the interpretation of images.
MCCHEAM316.topics: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Through critical readings of influential texts by figures such as Aby Warburg, Erwin Panofsky, Ernst Gombrich, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida, students explore the major ideas and methodologies that have shaped the field. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.

candidateDecisions.label: Biblical Languages and Exegesis
candidateDecisions.assessment: The Utrecht evidence independently confirms biblical studies, Greek, Hebrew and exegesis. Current UCR courses offer contextual, visual and literary methods but no sequence in biblical languages or scriptural interpretation. The detailed antiquity topics inherited from Groningen are not used to establish Utrecht requirements.

candidateDecisions.label: Practical Theology and Ministry Preparation
candidateDecisions.assessment: The current Utrecht target includes practical theology and a route preparing for the ministry master. UCR’s social science, psychology and communication courses do not supply practical theology, supervised pastoral practice or spiritual formation.

candidateDecisions.label: Groningen Theology Trajectory
candidateDecisions.assessment: The registry row describes a different offering. It is explicitly disposed of without generating UCR content for the Utrecht target.

analysis: One related-fields plan follows a question across philosophy of belief and ethics, history and visual and literary interpretation, then examines how worldviews and identities operate in public life. Art history supports the comparator’s aesthetics strand through introductory visual inquiry, West African arts, Mediterranean exchange, modern museums and historical interpretation of images. Literary close reading, myth and archaeology supply complementary approaches to texts and objects. Historical and qualitative research teach different ways to make warranted claims from sources. Rights, political authority, social psychology, sociology, media and conflict connect cultural traditions to contemporary institutions and disputes. Rhetoric and Argumentation share the practice of structured argument. General academic development, history and ethics remain complementary to theological research, Protestant history and dogmatics. Current offerings do not support a second plan with credible biblical-language or pastoral depth. A separate generic public-life or arts plan would lose the combination that sustains the closest related comparison. Pairwise distinctness does not apply to one selected option.
